lens: Statistics, conformal prediction and chance-constrained optimization. I checked the theorem statements against the code and the results, the exchangeability units, decision dependence, how the CIs are built, multiple testing, and whether conservativeness and OOD failures are reported honestly. Sources: docs/research_proposal.md, results/tables.md (v3, 60+60 fields), experiments/core.py, exp_lib.py, exp_main.py, exp_real.py, exp_cross2.py, exp_ablation.py, all figures/*.png, plus quick re-analyses of results/*.csv.
verdict: Reject in current form; resubmit after a major revision. The user's critique is correct, and from a statistics view it is worse than "comparing categories". Eleven of the 16 baselines take the same scalar score S on the same planner and return one number from that sample: an order statistic (Scenario = rank 96/100, Worst-case = rank 100/100, CE-U = rank 91/100), a moment rule (Gaussian, Cantelli) or a tail mean (CVaR, DRO-CVaR). Five of the 16 are pointwise strawmen that fail by construction. With a one-dimensional decision lambda, the chance constraint is exactly "lambda >= the (1-eps) quantile of S". So "CE-U is the least conservative valid method" follows from split-conformal exactness and is not an empirical finding. I checked this: scenario_lambda with beta=0.5 picks rank 90/100, next to CE-U's 91. The whole gap to the Scenario baseline (8.5% vs 6.7% overlap, about 0.6 passes per field) comes from Scenario certifying a stronger PAC (eps, beta=0.01) property. CVaR and DRO only make sense for multi-dimensional decisions; in 1-D they are dominated by definition. No competing planning algorithm appears: no terrain-aware CPP, no joint chance-constrained or SAA optimization over pass positions, no robust or tube MPC, no model-based Monte Carlo planner, and no modern conformal competitor (conditional, hierarchical, PAC, EVT). Separately: Theorem 1's upper bound is false as stated and the paper's own Fig 5 contradicts it. Theorem 2's dominance argument is unproven and has no measurable effect in any experiment. CE-A cannot differ from CE-U by construction (fitted slope coefficient b=0.000 for wheat; sigma varies about 1% for paddy). The simulator shares one RTK time index across all passes. The pooled Clopper-Pearson CIs ignore clustering. The real-robot "OOD failures" lie inside the exchangeable Beta-binomial envelope. What can be kept: the problem formulation, the pass-to-pass reduction (Lemma 1, whose absolute-error-score ablation is a genuine and convincing result) and the dimension-free certificate idea. To reach Q1, the paper needs to (1) turn the margin-rule comparison into a theorem, (2) spend the experiments on real algorithmic competitors in a richer decision space, (3) correct the theorems, and (4) report the statistics at the right level of exchangeability.

major_issues.issue: The baselines are not competing algorithms. They are 1-D functionals of the same score sample on the same planner, so the headline comparison is circular. In exp_main.py, Gaussian-on-score, Cantelli, Scenario, CVaR, DRO-CVaR and Worst-case all take scoresU, the same calibration scores CE-U uses. Scenario with discarding at d=1 picks an order statistic (n=100: rank 96 at beta=0.01, rank 94 at beta=0.1, rank 90 at beta=0.5; CE-U uses rank 91, checked numerically with exp_lib.scenario_lambda). It is the training-conditional/PAC version of conformal (Vovk 2012; Wilks 1941 tolerance limits). Five 'pointwise' rules (Gaussian pointwise, empirical pointwise, conformal pointwise, fixed 5/10 cm, slope rule) control a per-cross-section event and must fail on fields with thousands of cross-sections. They reach P(no miss) of about 0 to 0.33 and fill half of Fig 3.
major_issues.why_reviewer_would_reject: A conformal/CCO reviewer will note that once lambda is scalar, every valid rule satisfies lambda >= Q_{1-eps}(S) + o(1). Split conformal is known to be exact up to 1/(n+1), so the efficiency ranking is fixed in advance and decided by which guarantee (marginal vs PAC) each rule targets, not by the algorithm. A robotics or agricultural reviewer will say no coverage-planning algorithm was compared. Both conclude the experiments do not test the paper's contribution.
major_issues.concrete_fix: (a) Replace the margin-rule horse race with a short theorem: among symmetric, rank-invariant rules lambda(S_1..S_n) that are valid for all exchangeable distributions, the smallest is S_(ceil((n+1)(1-eps))). Add a PAC corollary (rank from the Binomial). Then show CE-PAC (beta=0.01) and Scenario d=1 coincide, and keep Gaussian/Cantelli/CVaR/DRO only in one appendix table. (b) Drop the pointwise strawmen to one row, or replace them with an honest valid pointwise method: Bonferroni over m cross-sections, or a Gaussian sup bound via the expected Euler characteristic (Adler & Taylor 2007). (c) Spend the main experiment on algorithmic competitors in a richer decision space (see competitor list): SAA-MILP and multi-dimensional scenario programs over per-pair spacings, terrain-aware 3D CPP, risk allocation, tube MPC, model-based Monte Carlo. Also include Fields2Cover as the base planner, with CE as a plug-in layer.
major_issues.effort: Theorem: about 1 day. Rerunning baselines: free, since the scores already exist. Competitors: 4-6 days (see list). Compute is feasible on 4 CPUs (v3 main run was about 15-40 min per crop).

major_issues.issue: Theorem 1 is mis-stated. It claims 1-eps <= Pr[M=0] <= 1-eps+1/(n+1). The proof only gives {M=0} ⊇ {S_{n+1} <= q}, so the upper bound holds for Pr[S<=q], not for Pr[M=0]. The repo's own E1 contradicts the stated bound: at target 0.70 the realized CE-U value is 0.775 (CE-A 0.766), above the bound 0.70+1/101=0.710. At 0.90 it is 0.922 vs 0.910. The 'theoretical band' in Fig 5 is drawn for the wrong quantity, and the report's claim that the certificate is 'tight' (§5.2, proposal §7) is unsupported: slack grows from about 2 to 7.5 points as eps grows.
major_issues.why_reviewer_would_reject: A stated theorem that the authors' own figure contradicts is an immediate credibility failure for a theory-plus-experiments paper.
major_issues.concrete_fix: Restate: Pr[S_{n+1}<=q] ∈ [1-eps, 1-eps+1/(n+1)] (no ties) and Pr[M=0] >= 1-eps. Log S_test for every test run (core.pair_scores is already available) and plot three curves per eps: Pr[S_test<=q], which must sit in the band; Pr[M=0]; and the gap split into (i) Lemma-1 sufficiency slack (polygon boundaries, masked passes) and (ii) plan-dominance slack (calibrating on pi_ref, which has more passes). This turns the conservativeness into an explained, quantified result.
major_issues.effort: About 0.5 day of code (add S to evaluate_plan output) plus one E1 rerun (12 fields × 4 eps × 4 draws, under 1 h).

major_issues.issue: Theorem 2 (plan-uniform dominance) and the fixed-point calibration are unproven in the setting used, and empirically inert. (1) The argument 'max over a subset <= max over the full set' holds only if pi_lambda's pair terms are a subset of pi_ref's. They are not: passes sit at different y, with different chord lengths on convex polygons, different terrain features, and (for CE-A) different sigma normalization. The argument needs A4 (stationarity in k), which contradicts the heterogeneity that motivates CE-A and Theorem 3. (2) calibrate_conformal (exp_lib.py:79-111) stops on a data-dependent rule and caps iterations at 3. If q > lam_ref after 3 iterations it returns q anyway, so dominance is not guaranteed and non-convergence is not logged. fp_iters=3 occurs on 14-26 of 60 fields. (3) Ablations: full vs naive per-field difference in P(no miss) is -0.0001 ± 0.037 (60 fields). In the hard regime, naive (0.918) ≈ full (0.921), and naive's median lambda is even larger (16.6 vs 16.0 cm). (4) Deployment: historical logs come from whatever plan was executed. Nobody can re-collect calibration data under a chosen reference plan, which the fixed-point procedure assumes by re-simulating at every iteration.
major_issues.why_reviewer_would_reject: 'Decision-dependent calibration' is in the title and listed as a key contribution. A theorem whose key step is false in general, and whose algorithm changes nothing measurable, will be judged unsupported or trivial.
major_issues.concrete_fix: (a) State the requirement as an explicit, testable assumption: for each lambda <= lambda_ref, S(pi_lambda) <=_st S(pi_ref), with test errors independent of the calibration data. Prove validity conditionally on the calibration set (q fixed implies pi_q fixed), then marginalize. Test the assumption with ECDFs of S under pi_lambda for a lambda grid vs pi_ref (one-sided KS), and show this as a figure. (b) Make the final quantile come from a fresh calibration split after lambda_ref is frozen, or take a union bound over iterations, and report non-convergence counts. (c) Put a real decision-dependent mechanism in the simulator so the theorem matters. For example, the line-acquisition transient after a headland turn should depend on pass spacing relative to the minimum turning radius (Pi-turn vs Omega/fishtail turn; Bochtis & Vougioukas 2008); currently d0 ~ N(0, 3 cm) regardless of plan (core.py:173). Show that naive calibration under-covers and the fixed point repairs it. (d) Cast the problem as feedback covariate shift (Fannjiang et al., PNAS 2022) and compare against it. Otherwise, demote Theorem 2 to a remark.
major_issues.effort: Theory rewrite: 1-2 days. Simulator turn-transient model and ablation rerun: 1-2 days.

major_issues.issue: CE-A is inert by construction, so 'CE-A = CE-U, one point in every plot' is the expected result, not a finding. Logs: wheat sigma-hat a=6.15 cm, b=0.000, so CE-A is exactly CE-U with different random draws. Paddy b=0.221 m per tan(slope): at 2° side slope, sigma rises from 5.06 to 5.12 cm (about 1%). Passes CE-A minus CE-U are 0 on 48/60 paddy fields, and the correlation of the overlap difference with slope is 0.19 (paddy) and 0.02 (wheat). The feature is also wrong by the paper's own Lemma 1. Uniform side-slope effects (antenna roll offset, mean slip) are common-mode in the field frame: core.py gives field-frame offset h·g·(1-c) for both directions. They cancel in e_{k+1}-e_k, so mean |side slope| cannot predict a pass-to-pass score. The SigmaModel.fit target (90th percentile of pair maxima on the nominal plan, exp_lib.py:44) is also ad hoc. CE-A has 50% higher E[miss] than CE-U on paddy (0.75 vs 0.50 ‱).
major_issues.why_reviewer_would_reject: An 'adaptive' variant that the data show is identical to the baseline, presented as a contribution with p=0.95 and 0.81 'no significant gain', reads as padding. Reviewers will ask why it is there.
major_issues.concrete_fix: (a) Use a location-scale normalized score (Lei et al., JASA 2018): S=(e_{k+1}-e_k-mu_k)/sigma_k. Here mu_k and sigma_k come from features that actually drive the differential error: the slope difference between adjacent passes or the terrain curvature (second difference of the DEM across passes), along-pass slope variability, and run covariates such as soil moisture, speed and controller. Fit them on a disjoint split, or learn them by minimizing erosion on a split (Cleaveland et al., AAAI 2024; Kiyani et al., NeurIPS 2024). (b) Show where adaptivity pays off: plot per-field paired gain (overlap_A - overlap_U) against a heterogeneity index, and run a controlled semi-synthetic sweep (DEM relief scaled ×1-×5, ridge/terrace fields) to find the threshold. (c) If there is still no gain on real fields, say in the abstract that CE-A reduces to CE-U on homogeneous terrain and move it to an extension. Use TOST equivalence, not 'p=0.95'.
major_issues.effort: 2-3 days (feature engineering, refit, semi-synthetic sweep on the existing fields).

major_issues.issue: A simulator artifact distorts exactly the statistics the paper is about. In core.simulate, all K passes of a run are integrated in parallel, and the RTK error uses the index ti=(rtk_offset+int(t·dt)) % nr with shape (R,1) (core.py:192). Every pass in a run therefore sees the same RTK time series at the same along-track time. Passes k and k+2 get the same RTK realization, and opposite passes get it mirrored. In reality passes are minutes apart. The error is also injected in the vehicle frame, so it flips sign in the field frame between directions. The series is one 1615 s, 1 Hz i2Nav car run (lag-1 autocorrelation 0.33, near-white). A pass needs about L/v ≈ 50 s, so each run uses one of roughly 30 distinct windows, and all 400 calibration/test runs per field reuse them. The 'heavy tail' (excess kurtosis 84) comes from one 2 s, 19 cm event, which hits all passes of a run at once when its window is drawn. This makes the number of independent pairs much smaller than N, which explains why N, and hence decision dependence, barely matters. It also makes the Gaussian-failure story rest on one event.
major_issues.why_reviewer_would_reject: The validity results hold by construction (i.i.d. Condition draws). The efficiency and decision-dependence conclusions, by contrast, depend on the pass-to-pass dependence structure the simulator gets wrong. A careful reviewer who reads core.py will discount all simulation conclusions except validity.
major_issues.concrete_fix: Index RTK by cumulative operation time: pass k starts at t_k = sum_{j<k}(L_j/v + t_turn). Project the ENU error (en, ee, already computed in data_rtk.py) onto the field lateral axis instead of the car's lateral axis. Add more RTK series: the i2Nav awesome-gins-datasets GitHub hosts several sequences, so check which are downloadable. Use a stationary block bootstrap (block of about 30 s) to create diversity, and report results with and without the single 19 cm event. Rerun E2 and the ablations, and keep the old results only as a sensitivity row.
major_issues.effort: 1 day of code. Reruns of E2 (2 crops) plus ablations take about 2-3 h of compute.

major_issues.issue: Statistical inference is at the wrong level. (1) The CI on P(no miss) is a pooled Clopper-Pearson over 60×300 runs. Runs within a field share one calibration set and one plan, so outcomes are clustered: per-field coverage sd is 0.031, which matches Beta(91,10)+Binomial(300) (sd 0.034). The real CI for CE-U paddy is about ±0.008, not ±0.004, so the reported CIs are about 2× too narrow. (2) The metric 'fields not significantly below target' (per-field one-sided binomial test) tests calibration-conditional coverage, which conformal does not guarantee. For an exact method about 45% of fields fall below 0.9. Reporting 93% for CE-U and 100% for Scenario rewards conservativeness and confuses readers, and no multiplicity correction is applied across 60 tests. (3) Wilcoxon p-values (2.6e-10) compare the overlap of invalid methods with CE-U, which is meaningless, and overlap is never compared at matched coverage. (4) A single seed and a single field-shuffle are used.
major_issues.why_reviewer_would_reject: Statistics reviewers check CI construction and the unit of exchangeability first. Pooled binomial CIs on clustered data, and a 'target met' metric for a guarantee the method does not make, are standard reasons for a major revision or reject.
major_issues.concrete_fix: Use a two-stage cluster bootstrap (fields, then runs within field) for every coverage and overlap CI. Replace the 'fields >= target' column with: (i) the per-field coverage ECDF overlaid on the theoretical Beta-binomial law of CE-U, Beta(ceil((n+1)(1-eps)), n+1-ceil(...)) convolved with Binomial(n_test); (ii) a CE-PAC column for readers who want per-deployment guarantees. Pre-specify two endpoints: non-inferiority of marginal coverage (margin 0.01, cluster bootstrap), and overlap among valid methods at matched realized coverage, using an oracle lambda* from 10^4 runs per field to report the 'price of certification'. Holm-correct only these. Repeat over at least 3 field-shuffle seeds.
major_issues.effort: About 1 day (make_tables.py, plus an oracle-quantile run of about 1 h).

major_issues.issue: The real-robot (CitrusFarm) evaluation uses the wrong unit of exchangeability and overstates both 'OOD failure' and 'real validation'. (1) The calibration units are 10 m segments of K-pass windows (SEG=10, exp_real.py). Several units come from the same passes, and the random split mixes windows from the same sequence into calibration and test. Test windows use stride 1 (exp_real.py:120), so they overlap K-fold and the effective n_test ≈ n_test/K. The '5-95% interval' across random splits is not a CI. (2) There are only 7 sequences and 123 passes, and block 13B holds 79 of them. (3) Lateral error sd is 36.5 cm (p95 |e| = 73 cm). That is consistent with manual driving in orchard alleys, not autosteer, and gives 30-85% overlap for a hypothetical 6 m implement. The reference is a lattice fitted to the same data. (4) The LOBO/LODO 'failures' (3/10 below 0.9, minimum 0.833) are consistent with exchangeability. I simulated Beta(cal) × Binomial(n_test/K): P(coverage <= observed) = 0.17-0.96 across the 10 splits, so neither failure nor robustness is shown. (5) ACI runs on 49 and 24 strips. The Gibbs & Candès (2021) bound (max(eps1,1-eps1)+gamma)/(gamma·T) ≈ 0.94 at T=49 is vacuous, and the static baseline never failed (0.000), so the online result shows nothing.
major_issues.why_reviewer_would_reject: The proposal itself says real data 'decides whether this gets into Q1'. Calling meter-level teleoperated traces on an imaginary implement 'real-robot validation', with leaky splits, will be spotted, and the OOD numbers will be misread either way.
major_issues.concrete_fix: Make the unit of exchangeability a whole sequence, or a block-day, and give leave-one-sequence-out results with the Beta-binomial envelope drawn on every bar. Use non-overlapping test windows, or report effective sample size. Rename the section 'real-trace stress test (meter-level, manually driven)'. Report the conformal envelope for OOD instead of 'fails 3/10'. For online use, run ACI, nexCP, DtACI and PID over many random stream orderings or on the long simulated drift, and drop the 49-strip claim. Keep looking for genuine agricultural autosteer logs on GitHub, GitLab, S3 or GCS (e.g. AgOpenGPS community logs, public robot-farm bags). If none are found, state this limitation in the abstract.
major_issues.effort: Re-split and envelopes: about 1 day. Searching for new real data: open-ended, availability unverified.

major_issues.issue: The CE-R / Theorem 4 risk certificate is impractical and compared unfairly. The CRC rule (n·R̂+B)/(n+1) <= alpha with B=1 needs n >= 1/alpha - 1 = 332 runs before any finite lambda is feasible at alpha = 0.003. With n=500 (exp_main.py:30, five times the n=100 the other methods get), B/(n+1) = 20‱ of the 30‱ budget goes to the finite-sample term. That fully explains the '4.5× conservative' result. The surrogate is evaluated on the reference plan's traces for every lambda (risk_lambda), so applying it to pi_lambda-hat needs the same unproven dominance as Theorem 2. CE-R is also plotted on the P(no-miss) axis, where it shows 0.001, which is misleading.
major_issues.why_reviewer_would_reject: A certificate that needs more than 300 operations on one field is not credible for agriculture, and an extra 5× data budget is an unfair comparison.
major_issues.concrete_fix: Give CE-R the same n as the others, or move it to cross-field pooled calibration where n in the hundreds is realistic. Add the PAC alternatives RCPS (Bates et al., JACM 2021, WSR/betting bound) and LTT (Angelopoulos et al.), and certify miss-probability and expected-miss together. Report the split alpha = empirical risk + B/(n+1). Prove the surrogate dominance or state it as an assumption, and plot CE-R only on an E[M] axis.

major_issues.issue: Theorem 3 (weighted CP plus fixed point) has three gaps: (i) the denominator dP_cal/dphi must be estimated, so validity is only approximate (Lei & Candès 2021 bounds); (ii) pairs within a calibration run are dependent, so pair-level exchangeability fails, which the authors admit; (iii) the monotonicity of T(lambda) is claimed but unproven, and the weights depend on lambda through the plan. The experiments weight on regional slope features that do not move S, since b≈0. 'Weighted CP gave no benefit' is therefore uninformative: no harmful shift was ever created.
major_issues.why_reviewer_would_reject: An unproven theorem with a null experiment under a non-harmful shift looks speculative.
major_issues.concrete_fix: Use hierarchical conformal (Dunn, Wasserman & Ramdas, JASA 2023; Lee, Barber & Willett, NeurIPS 2023) for the run→pair structure instead of 'one pair per run'. Prove monotonicity under a stated condition or drop the claim. Design a harmful covariate shift on a covariate that drives S in the simulator: calibrate on dry soil (moisture 0.1-0.4), test on wet (0.6-0.9), where roughness and slip scale with moisture. Show that unweighted CP under-covers and weighted, robust (Cauchois et al., JASA 2024) or conditional CP repairs it.

major_issues.issue: The certificate's scope differs from the implementation, and two code issues touch the sensitivity and hard-regime runs. Lemma 1 is stated for a rectangle with boundary terms only at passes 1 and N. The code uses convex polygons with x-dependent chord ends, a 1 m cross-section grid (not sup over s), and a headland assumed perfectly covered (M = P.buffer(-2w)); none of this appears in the theorem. core.py:359 hard-codes the pass mask as (ys > lo-3) & (ys < hi+3) while core.evaluate uses ±w. For w=1.5 m (hard regime, sensitivity) the score includes irrelevant pairs and is conservative. For w=12 m it can omit relevant pairs, so {S<=lambda} ⊆ {M=0} can fail. overlap_ratio uses centerline chord × w and goes negative at w=12 m (Fig 8c).
major_issues.why_reviewer_would_reject: Mismatches between the theorem and the code are exactly what a careful theory reviewer checks.
major_issues.concrete_fix: Change the 3 to w in core.py:359 and rerun the w-sweep and the hard ablation. State Lemma 1' for convex cells with x-dependent boundary terms (or prove the sufficient inclusion), and define the certificate on the evaluation grid explicitly or add a Lipschitz argument. Either simulate headland passes or state 'main-area certificate'. Compute overlap from the executed multiplicity on the same cross-section grid.
major_issues.effort: 0.5 day of code plus about 2 h of reruns; 1 day for theory text.

major_issues.issue: The realistic deployment setting is a side experiment, and conditional coverage is never examined. In-field calibration with n=100 past operations on the same field is unrealistic (a field is worked 1-4 times a year). The cross-field setting (E3b) uses 10 repeats × 30 test fields × 40 runs, reports only marginal coverage over fields, and shows CQR ≈ CE-U (paddy 0.922 at 7.8% overlap vs 0.925 at 6.9%). A pooled certificate can badly under-cover atypical fields (steep, small, wet), and that is the real risk.
major_issues.why_reviewer_would_reject: Reviewers will ask whether a new steep field gets 0.9 or 0.7, and the paper cannot answer.
major_issues.concrete_fix: Make cross-field calibration (1-3 runs per field, hierarchical CP) the primary experiment. Report coverage stratified by slope, area and moisture tertiles with cluster-bootstrap CIs. Add Mondrian and conditional conformal (Gibbs, Cherian & Candès; pip conditionalconformal 0.0.5 is on PyPI) as competitors for group-conditional validity. Raise to at least 30 repeats.

major_issues.issue: Overclaiming and stale artifacts. Fig 3 is stale: it was generated at 05:02, before the v3 runs finished at 05:16 and 05:29, and shows '19' and '10' fields where the tables show 60 and 60. Fig 6(b) is an empty panel. Fig 1 claims P(no miss) >= 1-eps inside the ACI loop, but ACI only gives long-run frequency. 'Heavy-tailed RTK' rests on one event. experiments_report.md describes v2 (40 fields, 11 methods) and gives different Wilcoxon p-values (0.23/0.69) from tables.md (0.95/0.81).
major_issues.why_reviewer_would_reject: Inconsistency between text, tables and figures signals an unreliable pipeline.
major_issues.concrete_fix: Regenerate every figure from one versioned results set with a single make target. Sync the report to tables.md. Reword the ACI and heavy-tail claims.

competitor_algorithms_requested.name: SAA / big-M MILP joint chance-constrained pass spacing
competitor_algorithms_requested.reference: Luedtke & Ahmed, SIAM J. Optim. 2008; Pagnoncelli, Ahmed & Shapiro, JOTA 2009
competitor_algorithms_requested.how_to_implement_here: Decision: per-pair spacings delta_k (or pass centres y_k) for fixed N, plus binaries z_i per calibration run with sum z_i <= floor(eps'·n). Constraint for run i, pair k, every cross-section: e^i_{k+1}(x) - e^i_k(x) <= w - delta_k + M·z_i (plus boundary terms). Objective: maximize the total width covered (fewest passes / least overlap). Solve with scipy.optimize.milp (HiGHS, available, scipy 1.18.1), sweeping N. Report out-of-sample coverage against n=20/50/100/500. Expected: it overfits at d≈30 with n=100, which is exactly where CE's dimension-free certificate wins, so the comparison is genuinely algorithmic.

competitor_algorithms_requested.name: Multi-dimensional scenario program with sampling-and-discarding (d = N-1 spacings)
competitor_algorithms_requested.reference: Calafiore & Campi, IEEE TAC 2006; Campi & Garatti, JOTA 2011
competitor_algorithms_requested.how_to_implement_here: Same LP as above without binaries: remove k scenarios greedily, and compute the (eps, beta) guarantee with the d-dependent bound. Show the required n grows with N while CE needs n >= 1/eps - 1. Also report the d=1 scenario (current baseline) and state its equivalence to PAC conformal.

competitor_algorithms_requested.name: Fields2Cover base planner (angle optimisation + boustrophedon/snake route)
competitor_algorithms_requested.reference: Mier, Valente & de Bruin, IEEE RA-L 2023 (pip fields2cover 2.1.0 is on PyPI here)
competitor_algorithms_requested.how_to_implement_here: Use F2C swath generation (brute-force angle by #swaths or length), headland generation and route order on the same 120 polygons. Compare: F2C nominal; F2C + manufacturer overlap; F2C + CE layer. This shows CE is planner-agnostic, and the angle change introduces genuine decision dependence.

competitor_algorithms_requested.name: Terrain-aware 3D coverage path planning (direction optimisation on DEM)
competitor_algorithms_requested.reference: Jin & Tang, J. Field Robotics 28(3), 2011 (also Trans. ASABE 2010 for 2D)
competitor_algorithms_requested.how_to_implement_here: Per field, search the driving angle 0-179° with the Jin-Tang cost (terrain-projected skip/overlap + turn cost) on the Copernicus DEM. Plan with their spacing rule and execute in the same simulator. This is the natural competitor to CE-A's terrain adaptivity.

competitor_algorithms_requested.name: Side-to-side 3D CPP minimising skip/overlap between swaths
competitor_algorithms_requested.reference: Hameed, la Cour-Harbo & Osen, Robotics and Autonomous Systems 76, 2016 (verify details)
competitor_algorithms_requested.how_to_implement_here: Compute swath spacing so adjacent footprints abut on the 3D surface (surface-geodesic offset from the DEM gradient) instead of the horizontal plane. Evaluate miss and overlap under the same execution model.

competitor_algorithms_requested.name: Gaussian risk allocation over pairs (iterative risk allocation)
competitor_algorithms_requested.reference: Ono & Williams, IEEE CDC 2008; Blackmore, Ono & Williams, IEEE T-RO 2011
competitor_algorithms_requested.how_to_implement_here: Model each pair's sup gap as Gaussian or Gaussian-process. Allocate eps_k across pairs (sum eps_k = eps, Boole) by IRA so per-pair erosion is optimized, then plan with per-pass h_k. Direct competitor to CE-pair (uniform Bonferroni) and CE-A.

competitor_algorithms_requested.name: Tube-based robust MPC / mRPI erosion
competitor_algorithms_requested.reference: Mayne, Seron & Raković, Automatica 2005; Raković et al., IEEE TAC 2005; Kayacan et al. tube NMPC for tractors (IEEE/ASME TMech 2015, verify)
competitor_algorithms_requested.how_to_implement_here: Linearize the lateral LQR-I closed loop (core._lqr_gains), bound disturbances (slip, RTK) from calibration data, compute an outer approximation of the mRPI set, and erode by its lateral half-width. This gives a control-side worst-case certificate to set against CE's planning-side probabilistic one, and tests the proposal's 'tube MPC coupling' claim.

competitor_algorithms_requested.name: Model-based Monte Carlo chance constraint (GP / hierarchical Bayes error model)
competitor_algorithms_requested.reference: Standard robotics practice; e.g. GP-based uncertainty in planning. Cite a specific chance-constrained GP planning paper after checking.
competitor_algorithms_requested.how_to_implement_here: Fit a GP or AR model of e_k(s) on calibration traces (sklearn GaussianProcessRegressor), draw 10^4 posterior-predictive runs, and set lambda at the MC (1-eps) quantile of S. Shows the cost of model misspecification on heavy-tailed or real traces.

competitor_algorithms_requested.name: PAC / training-conditional split conformal (CE-PAC)
competitor_algorithms_requested.reference: Vovk, ACML 2012 / Mach. Learn. 2013; Park et al., ICLR 2020
competitor_algorithms_requested.how_to_implement_here: Rank from the Binomial(n, eps) beta-quantile (identical to scenario_lambda at d=1). Report alongside CE-U so marginal and per-deployment guarantees are compared like with like.

competitor_algorithms_requested.name: Extreme-value-theory quantile of the run-level maximum
competitor_algorithms_requested.reference: Coles, An Introduction to Statistical Modeling of Extreme Values, 2001
competitor_algorithms_requested.how_to_implement_here: scipy.stats.genextreme.fit on S (block maxima), or a GPD fit to pointwise exceedances with an extremal index. Take the 1-eps quantile. This is the principled parametric competitor for a sup-score, much stronger than Gaussian-on-score.

competitor_algorithms_requested.name: Conditional conformal / Mondrian conformal
competitor_algorithms_requested.reference: Gibbs, Cherian & Candès, 'Conformal prediction with conditional guarantees', 2023 (pip conditionalconformal 0.0.5 on PyPI); Vovk, Gammerman & Shafer 2005
competitor_algorithms_requested.how_to_implement_here: Covariates: field slope statistics, adjacent-pass slope difference, moisture, controller, speed. Function class: group indicators for slope/moisture tertiles plus linear terms. Compare group-conditional coverage with CE-U and CQR in the cross-field setting.

competitor_algorithms_requested.name: Optimised score normalisation for sup-over-trajectory scores
competitor_algorithms_requested.reference: Cleaveland, Lee, Pappas & Lindemann, AAAI 2024 (LCP); Bai et al., ICLR 2022; Kiyani, Pappas & Hassani, NeurIPS 2024
competitor_algorithms_requested.how_to_implement_here: Learn per-pass weights sigma_k (or a sigma(phi) map) on split 1 by minimizing the conformal quantile or the erosion, then calibrate on split 2. This is the principled data-driven version of CE-A.

competitor_algorithms_requested.name: Copula conformal for multi-step / multi-pair targets
competitor_algorithms_requested.how_to_implement_here: Replace CE-pair's Bonferroni over N+1 terms with an empirical copula across pair terms. Compare overlap with CE-pair (11-12%) and CE-U (6.7%).

competitor_algorithms_requested.name: Hierarchical (two-layer) conformal prediction
competitor_algorithms_requested.reference: Dunn, Wasserman & Ramdas, JASA 2023; Lee, Barber & Willett, NeurIPS 2023
competitor_algorithms_requested.how_to_implement_here: Cross-field calibration using all runs per field (field → run, or run → pair), instead of discarding to one run per field.

competitor_algorithms_requested.name: Robust conformal under f-divergence shift
competitor_algorithms_requested.how_to_implement_here: Set the radius from between-block or between-day divergence of score distributions on CitrusFarm and between regions in the simulation. Compare with weighted CP and Scenario-PAC on LOBO/LODO and the harmful moisture shift.

competitor_algorithms_requested.name: Online conformal methods beyond ACI
competitor_algorithms_requested.reference: Barber, Candès, Ramdas & Tibshirani, Ann. Statist. 2023 (nexCP); Gibbs & Candès, JMLR 2024 (DtACI); Angelopoulos, Candès & Tibshirani, NeurIPS 2023 (conformal PID)
competitor_algorithms_requested.how_to_implement_here: Run them on the 400-operation moisture drift (fig9) over at least 20 seeds and report long-run miss frequency and overlap with bands. Use the code from the authors' GitHub repos (aangelopoulos/conformal-time-series), or reimplement in about 50 lines each.

competitor_algorithms_requested.name: Conformal prediction under feedback covariate shift
competitor_algorithms_requested.reference: Fannjiang, Bates, Angelopoulos, Listgarten & Jordan, PNAS 2022
competitor_algorithms_requested.how_to_implement_here: The plan induces a known shift in pass features (positions on the DEM). Compute exact likelihood-ratio weights, compare with the fixed-point reference-plan method, and use it in the decision-dependent regime with spacing-dependent turn transients.

competitor_algorithms_requested.name: Risk-controlling prediction sets / Learn-then-Test
competitor_algorithms_requested.reference: Bates, Angelopoulos, Lei, Malik & Jordan, JACM 2021; Angelopoulos, Bates, Candès, Jordan & Lei, 'Learn then Test' (arXiv 2021)
competitor_algorithms_requested.how_to_implement_here: Use a PAC UCB (WSR betting) on the surrogate loss, and certify P(miss) and E[M] together via LTT. Compare with CE-R at equal n.

competitor_algorithms_requested.name: Conformalized quantile regression (keep) with stronger learners
competitor_algorithms_requested.how_to_implement_here: Already in E3b and matches CE-U. Keep it, add features (moisture, curvature), and present it as a genuine competitor, not a strawman.
